name: pueue
title: Pueue
description: Manage the Pueue task queue daemon from Raycast: browse and act on tasks, follow live output, control groups and parallelism, and watch the queue from the menu bar.
author: da-wei_lee

commands.name: tasks
commands.title: Tasks
commands.description: Browse, filter, and act on Pueue tasks; view or follow their output.

preferences.name: showDetail
preferences.title: Detail Pane
preferences.label: Show the detail pane by default
preferences.description: Show task metadata and a log preview beside the list. Toggle at any time with ⌘I.

preferences.name: detailLogLines
preferences.title: Log Preview Lines
preferences.description: How many trailing log lines to show in the detail pane for the selected task. Higher values cost one extra `pueue log` call per selection change.

commands.name: add-task
commands.title: Add Task
commands.description: Queue a shell command with a working directory, group, label, priority, dependencies, and delay.

commands.name: quick-add
commands.title: Quick Add Task
commands.description: Queue a command straight from root search, using your last-used group and working directory.

commands.name: groups
commands.title: Groups
commands.description: List Pueue groups, pause or resume them, change parallelism, and add or remove groups.

preferences.name: showDetail
preferences.title: Detail Pane
preferences.label: Show the detail pane by default
preferences.description: Show each group's full breakdown — progress, average duration, estimated remaining, elapsed, and the ids that failed — beside the list. Toggle at any time with ⌘I.

commands.name: queue-menu
commands.title: Queue Menu Bar
commands.description: Show running, queued, and failed task counts in the menu bar with one-click actions.

preferences.name: titleCounts
preferences.title: Menu Bar Title
preferences.description: What number to show next to the icon. The title is hidden entirely when the chosen counts are all zero.

preferences.name: maxItemsPerSection
preferences.title: Items per Section
preferences.description: How many tasks to list under Running / Queued / Failed before collapsing into an "…and N more" item. Keeps a large queue from rendering hundreds of menu items every minute.

preferences.name: showGroups
preferences.title: Groups Section
preferences.label: Show a Groups section
preferences.description: Adds one submenu per group with pause / resume and a parallelism picker.

preferences.name: menuQuery
preferences.title: Menu Bar Query
preferences.description: Optional Pueue query applied to the menu bar's status read, e.g. "last 100". Useful when you keep thousands of finished tasks around. Leave empty for all tasks.

preferences.name: connectionCounts
preferences.title: Connection Counts
preferences.label: Show each connection's counts in the menu
preferences.description: Read every configured connection on each refresh so the Connection rows show that daemon's running, queued, and failed counts. Costs one extra read per connection per interval — cheap over a multiplexed SSH connection, but off by default because most setups have only one. An unreachable host degrades its own row and nothing else.

preferences.name: pueuePath
preferences.title: Pueue Binary Path
preferences.description: Absolute path to the `pueue` client. Empty = auto-probe /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, ~/.cargo/bin, ~/.local/bin. `pueued` is looked for beside it. Raycast runs under launchd with no shell rc, so a bare `pueue` is never on PATH.

preferences.name: configPath
preferences.title: Pueue Config Path
preferences.description: Absolute path to pueue.yml. Empty = let pueue use its default (~/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue.yml on macOS). Also used to locate the task_logs directory.

preferences.name: connections
preferences.title: Remote Connections
preferences.description: Separate connections with ';'. Simplest form is just an SSH host you can already reach - everything runs over ssh, nothing to set up: local_ubuntu. Add a label with 'name | ssh-host', and the remote pueue path if it is not on the non-interactive PATH (a cargo install is not): 'lab | local_ubuntu | ~/.cargo/bin/pueue'. Advanced: a config path as the second field selects a forwarded socket instead. Tip: paste rather than type. Raycast reloads the extension on every keystroke, so a half-typed host is briefly a real connection the extension tries to reach.

preferences.name: confirmDestructive
preferences.title: Confirmations
preferences.label: Confirm kill, remove, clean, and reset
preferences.description: Ask before destructive actions. In the view commands this is a confirmation dialog. The menu bar has no dialog available - a Raycast alert cannot show while the menu is open - so there the same setting hides those items behind the Option key instead. Turn this off and both go away.

tools.name: get-tasks
tools.title: Get Tasks
tools.description: List tasks in the pueue queue, optionally filtered by group, status, or a substring of the command. Use this to answer what is running, what is queued, and what has failed. Task ids are per-daemon, so pass `connection` when the question is about a remote machine.

tools.name: get-task-log
tools.title: Get Task Log
tools.description: Get one task's details together with the tail of its output. This is the tool for 'why did task N fail' — an exit code says that something failed, the log says why. Ids are per-daemon; pass the same `connection` the id came from.

tools.name: get-groups
tools.title: Get Groups
tools.description: Get per-group progress: how many tasks are done out of the total, the breakdown by state, the average duration, and an estimate of the time remaining. Use this for 'how far through is my batch' rather than counting tasks yourself.

tools.name: create-group
tools.title: Create a Group
tools.description: Create a new pueue group with its own parallelism limit. Needed before queueing into a group that does not exist yet — `add-task` fails outright on an unknown group. One group per batch is pueue's idiom: it is the unit that carries both the concurrency limit and the progress.

tools.name: add-task
tools.title: Queue a Task
tools.description: Queue a shell command on a pueue daemon, optionally in a group, with a label, a working directory, and dependencies on other tasks. The command runs through `sh -c`, so pipes and && work as typed. Always confirmed before it runs.

tools.name: kill-tasks
tools.title: Kill Running Tasks
tools.description: Stop running tasks — by id, by group, or everywhere. Killing by group or with `all` ALSO PAUSES the group, so nothing further starts until it is resumed. Always confirmed, and the confirmation names the tasks.

tools.name: restart-failed
tools.title: Restart Failed Tasks
tools.description: Run failed tasks again — by id, by group, or everywhere. By default this creates new tasks and the originals keep their logs; `inPlace` reuses the ids and OVERWRITES the previous output, so only use it when the logs are no longer needed. Always confirmed.

tools.name: clean-tasks
tools.title: Clean Finished Tasks
tools.description: Remove finished tasks and their logs from the queue, optionally limited to one group, and optionally sparing the failures with `successfulOnly`. Nothing running or queued is affected. Prefer `successfulOnly` unless the user has said they are done investigating the failures. Always confirmed.

ai.instructions: Pueue is a task queue. A daemon holds tasks; tasks belong to groups; a group has its own parallelism limit and its own Running/Paused state. Task ids are PER-DAEMON. Id 6 on `lab` and id 6 on `Local` are different tasks, so always carry the `connection` from the result you read an id out of. Never guess a connection name — if one is rejected, the error lists the real ones. Default to reading. Do not queue, kill, restart, or clean anything unless the user asked for that specific change; 'have a look at', 'analyse', 'why did this fail' and 'give me an overview' are all read-only requests. To diagnose a failure, read the log — an exit code says that something failed, not why. When several tasks failed with the same command and the same exit code, read two or three logs rather than all of them, then say the rest match. Reading twenty logs to report one cause is a waste of the user's time. `finished` counts every task the daemon is done with, successful or not. A failed task is finished. Say 'succeeded' or 'failed' rather than 'done' when the distinction matters. Estimated times are an average of what has already finished, not a model. Present them as approximate, and say so when a group's tasks are obviously not comparable. When cleaning, prefer `successfulOnly` unless the user has said they are finished with the failures — cleaning deletes logs, and a log the user still needed cannot be recovered. `restart` without `inPlace` creates new tasks and leaves the originals with their logs. `inPlace` reuses the ids and overwrites those logs. Never choose `inPlace` on your own; it is only right when the user says the old output no longer matters. If only the `Local` connection is visible but the user expects remotes, say that Raycast does not pass extension preferences to AI tools and that opening any Pueue command once refreshes the copy the tools read. Do not tell them they have no remotes configured. To submit a batch, put it in its own group — that is the only unit pueue tracks progress for. Create the group first if it does not exist; `add-task` fails on an unknown group. Queue one task per item rather than one task running a loop, so a single failure is visible and restartable on its own. Use `after` when the steps must run in order; without it a group with parallelism above 1 will run them at the same time.

evals.input: @pueue Give me an overview of every connection, then explain why anything failed. Don't restart or change anything.
@pueue What's running right now, and how long has each one been going?
@pueue Why did my failed tasks fail? Read the logs — don't fix anything yet.
@pueue Which group has the most failures, and do they share a cause?
@pueue How far through is each group, and roughly when will the queue be empty?
@pueue Restart every failed task in place, overwriting their old logs
@pueue Restart the failures as new tasks so the original logs are kept
@pueue Queue 'python process.py <file>' once per file for a.csv, b.csv and c.csv
@pueue Make a group called nightly that runs 2 at a time, then queue 'make clean', 'make build' and 'make test' into it
@pueue Queue 'npm test' on every connection, one task each
@pueue Clean up the successful tasks but keep the failures so I can still read them
